Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
# Summary of the 2015 Manifesto

This manifesto outlines policies organised around different life stages, from childhood through retirement.

## Economic Policy

The document emphasises deficit reduction through continued spending controls, targeting elimination of the structural deficit and eventually running a budget surplus. The plan includes £30 billion in fiscal consolidation through departmental savings, welfare reforms, and tackling tax avoidance. Commitments include no increases to VAT, National Insurance, or Income Tax rates, while raising the personal tax allowance to £12,500 and the higher rate threshold to £50,000.

## Regional Development

Significant investment is promised in northern infrastructure, including £13 billion for transport and creation of regional development hubs. Plans include devolution of powers to cities choosing elected mayors, business rates retention pilots, and development strategies for the Midlands, South West, and East of England.

## Infrastructure

The manifesto commits over £100 billion to infrastructure, including railway electrification, road improvements, High Speed 2, and superfast broadband coverage reaching 95% of premises by 2017.

## Employment and Business

Targets include creating two million jobs and three million apprenticeships. Business support measures include red tape reduction, small business rate reviews, and maintaining competitive corporate taxation. Youth unemployment would be addressed through stricter benefit conditions for 18-21 year olds.

## Welfare Reform

Proposals include lowering the household benefit cap to £23,000, freezing working-age benefits for two years, rolling out Universal Credit, and removing automatic Housing Benefit entitlement for young jobseekers.

## Immigration

Policies focus on reducing EU migration through welfare restrictions, including four-year residency requirements before claiming tax credits and child benefit. Non-EU immigration controls would continue through the existing cap system, with stricter student visa enforcement.

## Education

Every failing secondary school would become an academy, with 500 new free schools planned. Primary school funding would be protected, with tougher literacy and numeracy standards. University tuition would continue under the existing loan system, with the student number cap abolished.

## Healthcare

NHS spending would increase by £8 billion above inflation by 2020. Goals include seven-day GP and hospital access, same-day appointments for over-75s, and integration of health and social care services.

## Housing

Targets include 200,000 Starter Homes for first-time buyers under 40 at 20% below market price, extension of Right to Buy to housing association tenants, and continuation of Help to Buy schemes.

## Pensions and Retirement

The triple lock on state pensions would continue. Inheritance Tax thresholds for married couples would effectively rise to £1 million through a new residence allowance. Residential care costs would be capped.

## Constitutional Matters

Plans include introducing English votes for English laws, implementing Scottish devolution commitments, and holding an EU referendum by end of 2017.

## Defence and Foreign Policy

Commitments include maintaining armed forces strength, building four nuclear submarine replacements, meeting NATO's 2% spending target, and maintaining the 0.7% international development commitment.
